title: Retrieval Augmented Generation
text: Retrieval augmented generation reduces hallucination by grounding model answers in retrieved external documents. The model can cite evidence instead of relying only on parametric memory.

title: Limits of RAG
text: RAG systems still fail when retrieval returns irrelevant or incomplete documents. Poor retrieval can cause the generator to produce incomplete answers or unsupported claims.

title: Agent Specialization
text: Specialized agents divide a complex workflow into narrower roles such as search, synthesis, planning, and verification. This can improve traceability because intermediate outputs are easier to inspect.

title: Multi-Agent Risks
text: Multi-agent systems can introduce coordination overhead and error propagation. Mistakes in an early search or summary step may affect all downstream agents.

title: Evaluating LLM Factuality
text: Factuality evaluation often combines automatic metrics with human judgment. Citation checks, claim verification, and reference overlap are useful but incomplete proxies for answer quality.

title: Human Evaluation
text: Human evaluation can assess correctness, completeness, clarity, and whether citations actually support the claims they accompany.

title: Single-Agent Baselines
text: A single-agent baseline is important because it tests whether gains come from agent specialization rather than from more context, more retrieval, or different prompts.

title: Tool Use in Research Assistants
text: Research assistants often use tools for search, retrieval, summarization, and citation management. Tool outputs should be recorded so answers can be audited later.
